# Contract fixtures — v1

These 33 JSON files are **copies**, not originals. They are generated by
`shellvibe-server` and pinned there by
`tests/Feature/Api/V1/ContractFixturesTest.php`.

- Source repo: `shellvibe-server`
- Source path: `tests/Fixtures/contract/v1/`
- Copied at server commit: `cc4b2fecd1ba540a880049a6428241d66c1b741f`
  (branch `fix/entitlement-baseline-and-contract-fixtures`, on top of
  `98435f12e9be9c914d3702b7d0512ab02de4fb82`)

`sync.operations.pull.json` also carries `meta.has_more`, added so a client
paging through the operation log can tell a short page from a caught-up one.
An added field is backward compatible; a client that ignores it behaves as
before, except that it cannot page.

Three fixtures differ from what `main` last held, all from that branch:

- `billing.reconcile.json` — the `pro` capability list now carries
  `local_device_link`, because a paid plan no longer drops the free baseline.
- `error.unauthenticated.json` — was a 200 `/me` body captured with a stale
  bearer token; now the real `401` envelope.
- `error.not-found.json` — `details` is `{}`, which is what the server sends;
  the `[]` it used to show was an artefact of the fixture capture.

## Why they are here

The client cannot run against the server's test suite and the server cannot run
against the client's. A file is the only thing both sides can agree on. Every
response shape this app parses is decoded from one of these fixtures in a test,
so a decoder that drifts from the server's real output fails here rather than in
production.

Volatile parts are placeholders on purpose: `<ulid>`, `<timestamp>`, `<token>`.
Only the *shape* is pinned. A decoder must therefore not assume a ULID parses or
a timestamp is a real date — which is the correct thing to assume about a field
the server may change the value format of within v1.

## Re-syncing

When the server's contract changes, regenerate there and re-copy here:

```sh
# in shellvibe-server
UPDATE_CONTRACT_FIXTURES=1 php artisan test --filter=ContractFixturesTest

# in shellvibe
cp ../shellvibe-server/tests/Fixtures/contract/v1/*.json test/fixtures/contract/v1/
(cd test/fixtures/contract/v1 && shasum -a 256 *.json | awk '{print $2"  "$1}' > MANIFEST.sha256)
```

Then update the commit hash above and run `flutter test`. A failing decode test
after a re-sync is the whole point: it names the field that moved.

## MANIFEST.sha256

Guards against these copies being edited locally to make a failing decoder pass.
`contract_fixtures_test.dart` recomputes it. The manifest cannot detect *server*
drift — only a re-sync does that.
